(2) Such other criteria determined by the Secretary of Defense, or when appropriate by the Department or Agency, to be good and sufficient.

Whenever evidence is received under item 21, or 22, the applicant will be furnished with a comprehensive and detailed summary of the information as the nationality security permit. The Administrative Judge and Appeal Board may make a clearance decision either favorable or unfavorable to the applicant based on such evidence after giving appropriate consideration to any relevant information. If the applicant did not have an opportunity to confront such evidence, any final determination made by the Administrative Judge or the Appeal Board must be made only by the Secretary of Defense, or the Department or Agency, upon personal review of the case record.

A verbatim transcription may be made of the hearing. The appellant shall receive one copy of the transcript, less the exhibits, without cost.

The Administrative Judge shall make a written clearance decision after considering all relevant facts, policies, and conclusions in the case, including those in the SOR, and whether it is clearly consistent with the national security interest to grant or continue a security clearance for the applicant. The applicant and Department Counsel shall be provided with a copy of the clearance decision. In cases in which evidence is received under item 21, or 22, the Administrative Judge's written clearance decision may require detailed conclusions of national security.

If the Administrative Judge decides that it is clearly consistent with the national security interest for the applicant to be granted or to retain a security clearance, the Department Counsel shall notify the applicant of the decision. If the Department or Agency decides to revoke or revoke the application of a previously granted security clearance, the Department Counsel shall notify the applicant that these actions are being taken. The applicant may appeal the Administrative Judge's clearance decision.

If the Department Counsel may appeal the Administrative Judge's clearance decision by filing a notice of appeal with the Appeal Board within 15 days after the date of the Administrative Judge's clearance decision. A notice of appeal received after 15 days from the date of the clearance decision shall not be accepted by the Appeal Board, or designated Board Member, except for good cause. A notice of cross appeal may be filed with the Appeal Board within 10 days of receipt of the notice of appeal. An untimely cross appeal shall not be accepted by the Appeal Board, or designated Board Member, except for good cause.

After filing a timely notice of appeal, an appeal brief must be received by the Appeal Board within 60 days from the date of the notice of appeal. The appeal brief must state the decision being appealed, the basis wanted, and site specific portions of the case record supporting any alleged error. A brief if any, filed within 30 days from receipt of the appeal brief, is considered part of the appeal. A copy of any filed brief shall be sent to the applicant or Department Counsel, as appropriate.

For requests for extension of time for submission of briefs may be submitted to the Appeal Board or designated Board Member. The Appeal Board, or designated Board Member, shall respond to the submission. The Appeal Board, or designated Board Member, shall may enter an order controlling the administration of the appeal and may enter a ruling regarding an appeal in an appropriate case or vacate the order under a showing of good cause.

The Appeal Board shall make the determinations based on the parties to determine whether error occurred. Its scope of review shall be to determine whether the decision was made in accordance with the rules and regulations.

A, The Administrative Judge's findings or conclusions, as supported by such relevant evidence, as a reasonable mind might accept as sufficient, must be supported by a conclusion, in light of all the contrary evidence in the same record. In making this review, the Appeal Board shall consider all evidence to the credibility determinations of the Administrative Judge.

B, The Administrative Judge adhered to the procedures required by E.O. 10865, as amended and this part; or

C, The Administrative Judge's rulings or conclusions are arbitrary, capricious, or contrary to law.

33. The Appeal Board shall issue a written clearance decision addressing the material issues raised on appeal. The Appeal Board shall have authority to:

(a) Affirm the decision of the Administrative Judge;

(b) Remand the case to an Administrative Judge to correct identified error. If the case is remanded, the Appeal Board shall specify the action to be taken on remand; or
